newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends off on sloppy supply, shut Asia arb. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends off on sloppy supply, shut Asia arb. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]

text.p: NWE naphtha weakened on Thursday amid healthy supply, sickly crude prices and lower Asian prices, traders said.
Traders said at least two naphtha cargoes were on the market with one French refiner offering 18,000 tonnes out of Donge, and a second offering material out of Britain.
A Dutch end-user said he was bidding (corrects from "offering") $180 in the current climate.
Traders said weakening Asian prices were also pressuring the market.
"The arb's no longer open so the material has nowhere to go," one trader said.
Asian prices have tumbled over the past weak as the arrival of arbitraged cargoes from the West has put the local market under pressure.
In Singapore, May swaps fell to $21.30/$21.50 per barrelin late trade on Thursday from $21.70/$21.90 on Wednesday.
While in Tokyo, first-half June open-spec naphtha was assessed at $207.00/$208.00 per tonne, compared with late Wednesday's $213.00/$214.00.
Added to these factors, traders said that a few petrochemicals were due to go into turnaround in the next few weeks which would further dampen demand.
